questions.q: What were the dimensions of the gold statue that king Nebuchadnezzar made and set up on the Plain of Dura?
questions.a: The statue was sixty cubits tall and six cubits wide.

questions.q: Who did King Nebuchadnezzar send to assemble for the dedication of the statue?
questions.a: He sent messengers to assemble the satraps, the prefects, the governors, the counselors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the other officials of the provinces.

questions.q: Who came to the dedication of the statue that Nebuchadnezzar had made?
questions.a: The provincial governors, regional governors, and local governors, together with the counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates and all the high officials of the provinces came to the dedication.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar want those in attendance at the dedication to do?
questions.a: He wanted those in attendance to fall down and worship the golden statue when they heard the sound of the horns, flutes, lyres, zithers, harps, and bagpipes, and all kinds of music.

questions.q: What did the king command to happen to those who did not fall down and worship the statue when they heard all the instruments and the music?
questions.a: The king said that those who would not fall down and worship, at that very moment, would be thrown into a blazing furnace.

questions.q: What did the peoples, nations, and languages do when they heard the sound of the music?
questions.a: They fell down and worshiped the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

questions.q: Who brought accusations against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
questions.a: Certain Chaldeans came and brought accusations against them.

questions.q: What did the Chaldeans say to the king before they accused Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
questions.a: They wished the king a long life before making their accusation.

questions.q: What decree did the Chaldeans remind the king that he had made?
questions.a: They reminded him that he had decreed that everyone who heard the music must fall down and worship the golden statue.

questions.q: What did the Chaldeans say would happen to anyone who did not worship the statue?
questions.a: They said that person would be thrown into a blazing furnace.

questions.q: Who did not fall down and worship the statue?
questions.a: Certain Jews, their names being Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, would not fall down and worship the statue.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar command when he heard the accusation against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
questions.a: He angrily commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought before him, and they were brought before the king.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar ask Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
questions.a: He asked them if it was true that they did not serve his gods or worship the golden statue he had set up.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar tell Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego would happen if they refused to worship the statue?
questions.a: He told them they would immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace, and no god would be able to rescue them from his power.

questions.q: What did Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego tell the king?
questions.a: They told him that they did not need to answer him about this matter.

questions.q: What was the response of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego to the king when the king repeated the command to fall down and worship the statue, and stated the consequences if they did not follow the king’s command?
questions.a: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego responded that their God could and would keep them safe and rescue them from the blazing furnace. But even if not, they would not worship Nebuchadnezzar’s gods or prostrate themselves to the statue.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar command concerning Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego?
questions.a: Nebuchadnezzar ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than normal, and for Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego to be tied up and thrown into the furnace.

questions.q: How were Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego dressed when they were thrown into the furnace?
questions.a: They were bound in their cloaks, tunics, turbans, and other garments when they were thrown into the blazing furnace.

questions.q: What happened to Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego and the men who took them to put them in the furnace?
questions.a: The men who took up Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were killed by the very hot flames from the furnace and Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego fell into the furnace.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar ask his counselors after he saw something amazing in the furnace?
questions.a: He asked them if they had not thrown three men, bound, into the fire, and they answered that it was true.

questions.q: What caused Nebuchadnezzar to be amazed and stand up quickly?
questions.a: Nebuchadnezzar was amazed because he saw four men, not tied up, walking around in the fire and they were not hurt and the brilliance of the fourth man was like a son of the gods.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar say to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego at the door of the furnace?
questions.a: He called for the servants of the Most High God to come out, and they came out of the fire.

questions.q: What did those present observe about Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego after they came out of the fire?
questions.a: Those present observed that the fire had not hurt their bodies; the hair on their heads was not singed; their robes were not harmed; and there was no smell of fire on them.

questions.q: What did Nebuchadnezzar say about the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
questions.a: He said that God was blessed because he sent his angel and rescued his servants, who were willing to give up their bodies rather than serve or worship any other god.

questions.q: What decree did Nebuchadnezzar issue after the event of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego and the blazing furnace?
questions.a: Nebuchadnezzar decreed that anyone from any people, nation, or language who spoke against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego would be cut into pieces and their house destroyed, because no other god is able to save like this one.

questions.q: What did the king do for Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego?
questions.a: Nebuchadnezzar, the king, promoted Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the province of Babylon.

commentary.text: Nebuchadnezzar's golden image. (Dan. 3:1-7) Shadrach and his companions refuse to worship it. (Dan. 3:8-18) They are cast into a furnace, but are miraculously preserved. (Dan. 3:19-27) Nebuchadnezzar gives glory to Jehovah. (Dan. 3:28-30)

Dan. 3:1-7 In the height of the image, about thirty yards, probably is included a pedestal, and most likely it was only covered with plates of gold, not a solid mass of that precious metal. Pride and bigotry cause men to require their subjects to follow their religion, whether right or wrong, and when worldly interest allures, and punishment overawes, few refuse. This is easy to the careless, the sensual, and the infidel, who are the greatest number; and most will go their ways. There is nothing so bad which the careless world will not be drawn to by a concert of music, or driven to by a fiery furnace. By such methods, false worship has been set up and maintained.

Dan. 3:8-18 True devotion calms the spirit, quiets and softens it, but superstition and devotion to false gods inflame men's passions. The matter is put into a little compass, Turn, or burn. Proud men are still ready to say, as Nebuchadnezzar, Who is the Lord, that I should fear his power? Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego did not hesitate whether they should comply or not. Life or death were not to be considered. Those that would avoid sin, must not parley with temptation when that to which we are allured or affrighted is manifestly evil. Stand not to pause about it, but say, as Christ did, Get thee behind me, Satan. They did not contrive an evasive answer, when a direct answer was expected. Those who make their duty their main care, need not be anxious or fearful concerning the event. The faithful servants of God find him able to control and overrule all the powers armed against them. Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst. If He be for us, we need not fear what man can do unto us. God will deliver us, either from death or in death. They must obey God rather than man; they must rather suffer than sin; and must not do evil that good may come. Therefore none of these things moved them. The saving them from sinful compliance, was as great a miracle in the kingdom of grace, as the saving them out of the fiery furnace was in the kingdom of nature. Fear of man and love of the world, especially want of faith, make men yield to temptation, while a firm persuasion of the truth will deliver them from denying Christ, or being ashamed of him. We are to be meek in our replies, but we must be decided that we will obey God rather than man.

Dan. 3:19-27 Let Nebuchadnezzar heat his furnace as hot as he can, a few minutes will finish the torment of those cast into it; but hell-fire tortures, and yet does not kill. Those who worshipped the beast and his image, have no rest, no pause, no moment free from pain, Rev. 14:10,11. Now was fulfilled in the letter that great promise, Is. 43:2, When thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned. Leaving it to that God who preserved them in the fire, to bring them out, they walked up and down in the midst, supported and encouraged by the presence of the Son of God. Those who suffer for Christ, have his presence in their sufferings, even in the fiery furnace, and in the valley of the shadow of death. Nebuchadnezzar owns them for servants of the most high God; a God able to deliver them out of his hand. It is our God only is the consuming fire, Heb. 12:29. Could we but see into the eternal world, we should behold the persecuted believer safe from the malice of his foes, while they are exposed to the wrath of God, and tormented in unquenchable fires.

Dan. 3:28-30 What God did for these his servants, would help to keep the Jews to their religion while in captivity, and to cure them of idolatry. The miracle brought deep convictions on Nebuchadnezzar. But no abiding change then took place in his conduct. He who preserved these pious Jews in the fiery furnace, is able to uphold us in the hour of temptation, and to keep us from falling into sin.
